content.content:
The user asks: "Who was the head of government in the countries that won each of the last 5 FIFA World Cups at the time of their victories?" Need to list the last 5 FIFA World Cups winners (most recent to older) and for each, identify the head of government (likely prime minister or president, depending on the country's system) at the time of the World Cup victory.

World Cups are held every 4 years. As of now (2025), the most recent was 2022 (Argentina), then 2018 (France), 2014 (Germany), 2010 (Spain), 2006 (Italy). Those are the last 5.

We need head of government at the time of each victory. For each country, find who was the head of government in that year.

- Argentina 2022: Head of government is President (Argentina's head of state and government). In 2022, President was Alberto Fernández (served from Dec 2019 to Dec 2023). So answer: Alberto Fernández.

- France 2018: France's head of government is Prime Minister (since president is head of state). In 2018, Prime Minister was Édouard Philippe (served May 2017 - July 2020). So answer: Édouard Philippe.

- Germany 2014: Germany's head of government is Chancellor. In 2014, Chancellor was Angela Merkel (served 2005-2021). So answer: Angela Merkel.

- Spain 2010: Head of government is Prime Minister (Presidente del Gobierno). In 2010, the Prime Minister was José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero (served 2004-2011). So answer: José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero.

- Italy 2006: Head of government is Prime Minister. In 2006, Prime Minister was Romano Prodi (served May 2006 - May 2008). Actually Italy had a change: In 2006, Prodi became PM after the election in April; he took office on 17 May 2006. So at the time of the World Cup final (12 July 2006), Prodi was PM. So answer: Romano Prodi.

We could also include date of victory.

Thus produce a list.

Potential nuance: For Argentina, some might argue head of government is President, which is correct. Provide names and maybe party.

Thus answer.

Check if any other nuance: maybe the user expects "head of government" meaning prime minister for parliamentary systems, president for presidential systems. So list accordingly.

Provide citations? Not required but could mention. Since we have no tool needed, we can answer directly.

Thus produce final answer.

content:
**Last 5 FIFA World Cup winners and the heads of government in those countries at the moment each title was secured**

| World Cup (year) | Winning country | Date of victory* | Head of government at that time | Title of the office |
|------------------|----------------|------------------|--------------------------------|----------------------|
| 2022 | **Argentina** | 18 July 2022 (final) | **Alberto Fernández** | President of Argentina (head of state + government) |
| 2018 | **France** | 15 July 2018 (final) | **Édouard Philippe** | Prime Minister of France (head of government) |
| 2014 | **Germany** | 13 July 2014 (final) | **Angela Merkel** | Chancellor of Germany (head of government) |
| 2010 | **Spain** | 11 July 2010 (final) | **José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero** | Prime Minister of Spain (Presidente del Gobierno) |
| 2006 | **Italy** | 9 July 2006 (final) | **Romano Prodi** | Prime Minister of Italy (Presidente del Consiglio) |

### Brief notes

- **Argentina (2022)** – The Argentine system is presidential; the President is both head of state and head of government. Alberto Fernández was in office from 10 December 2019 until 10 December 2023.
- **France (2018)** – France operates under a semi‑presidential system. While the President (Emmanuel Macron) is the chief of state, the Prime Minister (Édouard Philippe) is the head of government.
- **Germany (2014)** – Germany’s Chancellor is the chief executive. Angela Merkel had been Chancellor since 2005 and remained so until 2021.
- **Spain (2010)** – The Spanish Prime Minister (Presidente del Gobierno) is the head of government; José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero held the post from 2004‑2011.
- **Italy (2006)** – Italy’s head of government is the Prime Minister (Presidente del Consiglio). Romano Prodi took office on 17 May 2006 and was Prime Minister when Italy won the World Cup on 9 July 2006.

\*The “date of victory” refers to the date of the World Cup final in which the title was clinched.
